questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from that lane.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before you turn.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap large enough for you to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Sudden, unsafe lane changes.
How many passengers are in their car.
Their tendency to drive slowly.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers' actions. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest way to handle an aggressive driver is to stay away from them.

questions.question: Children on bicycles need extra space from motor vehicles because:

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware of children on bikes on the sidewalk—they may suddenly ride onto the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks where a no passing zone begins.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp ahead.
Road gets wider.
Right lane ends.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending and that merging traffic may be coming.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down gradually without using the brake.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull over to the side when it is safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazardous material trucks.
Watch for trains coming from multiple directions.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme care. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: May you leave a vehicle running if all occupants have left it?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you will only be away for a couple minutes.
Yes, if you will be away for less than an hour.

questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine and take the key out of the ignition when leaving a vehicle. Always lock your vehicle when you leave it, even for a short time.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road.
Only watch the center of the road.
Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around their car—the sides, front, and back. You need to know what is happening everywhere around your vehicle.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is when anything takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction can cause you to miss important signs and sounds that help you avoid crashes.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you drive better.
Make you feel better.
Hurt your judgment.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, being sleepy slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: A car ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass the car at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and move only after all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and move only after all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a car that is stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians you cannot see may be crossing. Stop and go only after all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: As blood alcohol content (BAC) goes up, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, you should slow down:

options.text: Only if you want to.
Before entering the curve.
Halfway through the curve.

questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. This way you will not need to brake hard while in the curve. Hard braking in a curve can cause your car to skid and become hard to control.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.explanation: Your safety and others' safety depends on what you do before driving. Before moving, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt, and secure all items. Do not adjust your mirrors while your car is moving.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only yield the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming cars are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming cars are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are going. They may seem slower than they really are. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are not sure about an oncoming car's speed, wait until it passes and there is enough space for you to change lanes safely.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
Area for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It may frustrate drivers behind you, causing them to pass unsafely. Drive with the flow of traffic at or below the speed limit.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Fight the drowsiness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest rest area to rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for real rest.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many crashes. Always drive with traffic flow at legal speeds.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already inside it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, no right turns are allowed.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Eating, drinking coffee, or showering will not speed this up.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of medication that impairs your driving is permitted:

options.text: Never.
If you don't feel drowsy.
If a doctor prescribed it.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers frustrated about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests to guide you safely through.

questions.question: When leaving a parallel parking space on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Turn on the appropriate turn signal.
Look over your shoulder.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Turn on your turn signal in the direction you are moving, and look over your shoulder toward traffic before entering the road.
